fixtures.name: fail-fast
fixtures.description: Promise.all over 8 calls; the second fails immediately
fixtures.note: per-policy succeeded and cancelled_before_dispatch counts are reported, not asserted, because they depend on when the guest's error reaches the host. The host learns of the failure first, replies to the guest, and, under rolling and sequential dispatch, refills the freed slot in the same step, before the guest can react; batch waits for its whole batch. The guest reports its error after one reply round trip, the host cancels queued calls, and it keeps collecting calls already dispatched, so a run ends when its last dispatched call finishes: about 120 ms after the first dispatch for batch and rolling, and about 240 ms for sequential, whose refill started a third 120 ms call. A guest error that took longer than a running call to arrive would let more calls start.

fixtures.name: deadline
fixtures.description: 12 calls (one 700 ms, eleven 200 ms) against a 540 ms run deadline
fixtures.note: reported, not asserted, because the split depends on startup. With 0 to about 130 ms from run start to first dispatch, expect sequential unknown=1, cancelled_before_dispatch=11; batch succeeded=3, unknown=1, cancelled_before_dispatch=8; rolling succeeded=6, unknown=4, cancelled_before_dispatch=2. All calls are admitted within startup, far ahead of the deadline.
